::: {#or-fusion}
| Platform Combinations | Soil Moisture Monitoring Specifics | Sensors and Technologies Used | Processing Method and Key Findings | Sources |
|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|---------------|
| **In-situ Only (Ground Networks)** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/in-situ.png){width=60} | Highly accurate point data, moisture profile measurements at different depths in the root zone (SMC, VWC). | TDR (Time-Domain Reflectometry), FDR, Capacitance Sensors, Tensiometers, Neutron Probes, WSN/IoT Networks. | Provide absolute "truth" for models, but do not scale well to large areas due to high logistical costs and local soil heterogeneity. | @Bogena2022, @Haokip2025, @Loconsole2025, @P2025 |
| **Satellites Only** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/sat.png){width=60} | Surface Moisture Monitoring (SSM) over large areas. | Microwave radars (SAR - Sentinel-1, SMAP), GNSS-R reflectometry, optical/thermal sensors (Sentinel-2, Landsat). | Microwaves penetrate clouds but have coarser spatial resolution. Optical data is affected by cloud cover and the signal is often suppressed by dense vegetation. | @Mkhwenkwana2025, @P2025, @Pablos2025 \* |
| **UAV only** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/drone.png){width=60} | Provides ultra-high (centimeter) resolution at the field level and allows flying below clouds. | Multispectral, hyperspectral and thermal cameras, miniaturized ground penetrating radars on drones (UAV-GPR). | Optical sensors monitor stress in plants, while technologies like UAV-GPR can directly map dielectric constant and moisture in the root zone without soil contact. | @Dong2024, @Haokip2025, @Kashyap2021, @Zhang2024 |
| **Satellites + In-situ** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/sat.png){width=60} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/in-situ.png){width=60} | Calibration of satellite surface moisture estimates and their connection with deeper root zone moisture. | Connection of satellite radar (SAR) and optical data with continuous measurements from IoT sensor networks. | Ground data is used to validate, correct satellite measurements and refine hydrological models. | @Mkhwenkwana2025, @P2025 |
| **Drones + In-situ** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/drone.png){width=60} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/in-situ.png){width=60} | Obtaining accurate high-resolution SMC. | UAV imaging supplemented with simultaneous measurements from soil TDR and capacitive sensors. | Machine learning connects surface manifestations captured by drone with the actual state of the soil in deeper layers. | @Haokip2025, @Zhang2024 |
| **Satellites + Drones** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/sat.png){width=60} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/drone.png){width=60} | Downscaling that refines coarse satellite maps. | Combination of satellite SAR (C-band) or optics (Sentinel) with multispectral and thermal imaging from UAVs. | UAVs provide detailed data even in cloudy conditions, while satellites provide a broader context and time series. | @Bazrafkan2025, @Teixeira2025 |
| **Satellites + Drones + In-situ** <br>![](../80_figures/81_icons/sat.png){width=60} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/drone.png){width=60} ![](../80_figures/81_icons/in-situ.png){width=60} | The most advanced predictive models, full 3D fusion and so-called Digital Twins. | Space-Air-Ground networks; IoT probes in the soil + autonomous UAV swarms + satellite constellations connected via Cloud and artificial intelligence. | In-situ networks deliver real-time accuracy, drones provide final detail and satellites global patterns. Deep learning models help predict drought and plan irrigation. | @P2025, @Saki2025, @Tsaousidis2026 |
